facts.text: The Fresh Earth Token is a unique combination of several different token archetypes, including utility, governance, community, asset-backed, and stablecoin.
The Fresh Earth Token facilitates communication and collaboration between farmers, investors, government bodies, and other stakeholders in the regenerative agriculture ecosystem.
The Fresh Earth Token has a decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) governance structure that allows for transparent and democratic decision-making processes.
The Fresh Earth Token is structured as a community token.
The Fresh Earth Token is described as a store of value that can be held by stakeholders as a liquid financial reservoir.
The value of the Fresh Earth Token is linked to the success of the ecosystem and the impact of regenerative projects.
In Token Classification, the Fresh Earth Token is a Utility Token that functions as a governance token.
The Fresh Earth Token is structured as a community token and an asset-backed token.
The underlying value of the Fresh Earth Token is based on fractional ownership, impact validation, and an economic engine built into the ecosystem.
The Fresh Earth Token’s assets include real-world assets, key performance indicators, and access and participation linked to the ecosystem’s ability to promote sustainable practices.
The Fresh Earth Token is intended to address climate change, health, and food security.
Share-like value for the Fresh Earth Token includes fractional ownership, rights and privileges, and impact leverage.
The Fresh Earth Token is intended to internalize the costs of the food system and redistribute money back into the ecosystem through token sales and rewards.
Network value for the Fresh Earth Token is built on trust and utility, supply and demand, and network growth.
The Fresh Earth Token is built on the Hashgraph HTS (Hedera Hashgraph Token Service) platform.
The Fresh Earth Token uses Guardian nodes from the Hedera network.
The Fresh Earth Token serves as fractional ownership, a means of access, a medium of exchange, a governance tool, and a store of value within the ecosystem.
The Fresh Earth Token is described as a decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) that manages the food ecosystem business.
The Fresh Earth Token is governed by smart contracts and controlled by token holders.
The Fresh Earth Token is described as having a finite supply determined by the ecosystem’s needs and growth.
The Fresh Earth Token is designed to be divisible to allow fractional ownership and increased accessibility.
The Fresh Earth Token has a symbiotic relationship with regenerated land and the health of people.
The Fresh Earth Token is described as a utility token that allows holders to access and participate in products, services, a knowledge base, and a rewards system.
The Fresh Earth Token is described as a governance token governed by smart contracts controlled by token holders.
The Fresh Earth Token is described as a digital collaborative community that empowers individuals and businesses to take control of their food sources and improve quality and nutritional density.
The Fresh Earth Token community includes participation in Fresh Earth Projects, advocacy groups, Buying Groups, and Research Groups.
The Fresh Earth Token is described as an asset-backed token representing fractional ownership of the ecosystem.
The Fresh Earth Token is valued based on the assets of the ecosystem and the impact of regenerative projects.
The Fresh Earth Token’s underlying value is tied to monetizable value of carbon sequestration, biodiversity, water retention, and food nutritional density.
The Fresh Earth Token uses key performance indicators (KPIs) to provide verified measurements of impact.
The Fresh Earth Token’s KPIs are described as enabling external funding from government schemes such as carbon trading.

The Fresh Earth Token is described as enabling access to markets including carbon offsetting, pay for performance, impact investing, community-based financing, regenerative agriculture financing, water rights trading, biodiversity offsets, ecosystem services markets, conservation easements, benefit-sharing agreements, and community land.
The Fresh Earth Token is described as having stablecoin characteristics as an assets-based fractional ownership token linked to the mentioned asset values.
The Fresh Earth Token is described as having an asset-to-token ratio that can buy back tokens if needed to maintain value.
The Fresh Earth Token is described as representing fractional ownership of the ecosystem for investment without purchasing the entire ecosystem.
The Fresh Earth ecosystem includes an impact validation system that uses data to measure and validate the impact of regenerative practices.
The Fresh Earth ecosystem is designed to internalize the costs of the food system and redistribute money back into the ecosystem through token sales and rewards.
The Fresh Earth ecosystem includes real-world assets such as carbon credits, biodiversity, and water retention.
The Fresh Earth ecosystem includes food nutritional density as a real-world asset.
The Fresh Earth ecosystem is described as owning or having JV and licensing relationships with regenerative farming and production systems.
The Fresh Earth ecosystem includes IP such as key performance indicators (KPIs) used to measure and verify impact.
The Fresh Earth ecosystem includes a B2B and B2C marketplace, a digital collaborative community, and a rewards system.
The Fresh Earth ecosystem aims to create a transparent and verifiable impact for sustainable agrifood projects to build trust and utility.
The Fresh Earth ecosystem uses blockchain technology to provide a secure and decentralized platform.
The Fresh Earth ecosystem aims to balance supply and demand for regenerative food products through its B2B and B2C marketplaces.
The Fresh Earth ecosystem aims to increase supply of regenerative food products by connecting regenerative farmers with businesses and consumers.
The Fresh Earth ecosystem aims to incentivize participation and engagement through its rewards system to drive demand for the Fresh Earth Token.
The Fresh Earth ecosystem includes networks including B2C, B2B, digital communities of consumers and experts, farm and supplier networks, and health practitioners.
The Fresh Earth ecosystem is described as using incentive drivers such as the rewards system and the validation system to promote network growth.
The Fresh Earth ecosystem is described as following a positive feedback loop where success drives more investment and greater impact, leading to greater value for token holders.
Fresh Earth consumers are described as incentivized and rewarded for participation to drive network growth and increase token value.
The Fresh Earth ecosystem is described as using Metcalfe's Law to accelerate growth of the network.
The Fresh Earth Token is described as representing fractional ownership of the Fresh Earth ecosystem, with each token representing an individual’s fractional ownership.
The Fresh Earth Token is described as including monetizable regenerative value of a hectare of land and health of a person.
Holders of the Fresh Earth Token have voting power in governance decisions.
Holders of the Fresh Earth Token have access to discounted prices on regenerative food products.
Holders of the Fresh Earth Token have access to the digital collaborative community.
The Fresh Earth Token is described as potentially providing rewards for participating in validation of KPIs, purchasing Fresh Earth food products, referrals, or being a Fresh Earth ambassador.

The Fresh Earth token is described as leveraging future impact measured by KPIs to secure external funding from carbon offsetting, pay for performance, impact investing, community-based financing, regenerative agriculture financing, water rights trading, biodiversity offsets, ecosystem services markets, conservation easements, benefit-sharing agreements, and community land trusts.
External funds from the Fresh Earth token are described as redistributed back to stakeholders as rewards for participation.
Fresh Earth tokens are described as having a right to use to access services and content within the ecosystem.
Fresh Earth tokens are described as having a right to vote to influence decision-making of the DAO that manages the Fresh Earth ecosystem.
Fresh Earth tokens are described as having a unit of account function to measure value of services, assets, labor, and liabilities within the ecosystem.
Fresh Earth tokens are described as having a medium of exchange function to trade goods or services within the ecosystem.
Fresh Earth tokens are described as having a store of value function that may retain value and purchasing power over time.

The Fresh Earth ecosystem is described as incentivizing participation and engagement through incentive drivers including Get Access, Get Discount, Get Revenue, Get Reward, and Participate in Governance.
The Fresh Earth ecosystem is described as having an Appreciation Potential that allows token holders to benefit from ecosystem success or token value uplift by holding, staking, or selling tokens.
Fresh Earth Tokens are described as being used as a means of access to services and content such as marketplaces for regeneratively produced food and resources for regenerative farmers.
Fresh Earth Tokens are described as being used for participation in governance, allowing token holders to vote on key decisions and proposals.
Fresh Earth Tokens are described as serving as a unit of account and medium of exchange within the ecosystem for measurement and intermediation of economic transactions.
Fresh Earth Tokens are described as acting as a store of value with value tied to success and growth of the ecosystem.
